results.content: # Fed’s preferred inflation gauge shows core prices rose 3.3% annually in July. Jeff Cox@jeff.cox.7528@JeffCoxCNBCcom. Prices consumers pay for a variety of goods and services rose slightly in July, according to the Federal Reserve's main inflation gauge. The personal consumption expenditures price index, which the Fed uses as its preferred forecasting tool, increased a seasonally adjusted 0.2% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.7%, the Commerce Department reported Wednesday. Both were 0.1 percentage point above the Dow Jones consensus. But stripping out volatile food and energy costs, core PCE posted respective gains of 0.2% and 3.3%, in line with forecasts. results.content: # Fed’s Preferred Inflation Meter Unchanged In July—Here’s Why Interest Rates Hikes Are Now More Likely. The Federal Reserve’s favored inflation reading was unchanged in July, according to federal data reported Wednesday, as central bank officials have signaled interest rate hikes unless they see improvements to consumer price increases. Annual inflation was 3.3% in July, according to core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index data published Wednesday by the Bureau of Economic Analysis, falling above consensus analyst estimates of 3.2% and matching June’s price increases.
